newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan telecom sector to allow more foreign access.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan telecom sector to allow more foreign access.

text.p: Taiwan has drafted rules to liberalise foreign ownership of basic telecom services by raising the legal limit to 30 percent from 20 and allowing even greater indirect control, officials said on Thursday.
"The ministry is proposing to change the limit on foreign investment in Taiwan's telecom businesses," an official at Ministry of Transportation and Communications said.
The amendment requires cabinet approval, which the official called likely, followed by a review in parliament that analysts said could be contentious.

The ceiling on foreign ownership in telecoms has been a key obstacle in bilateral negotiations with the United States and other telecom powers over Taiwan's long-frustrated bid to enter the World Trade Organisation.
Analysts have said the government's reluctance to ease the limits reflected a desire to give longtime monopoly Chunghwa Telecom time to prepare for international competition.
Taipei also has cited national security concerns.

The official said the ministry on Wednesday issued draft rules to amend Taiwan's telecom laws, which now allows foreign interests to own only 20 percent of ventures offering basic "common-carrier" telephone services,
Common-carrier services are the main telephone and data lines in Taiwan's telecom network, including mobile telephone and retail telephone services.
Under the amendment, foreign investors would be able to hold up to 30 percent of a common-carrier venture outright and a further 20 percent indirectly, the official said.
Indirect control could be achieved by investing through a locally controlled joint venture, officials said.
Communication ministry officials said Taiwan would remove an 11.5 percent cap on telecom profits by end-1997, complying with a deal reached in July 1996 with U.S. trade negotiators.
The profit cap, which had been implemented to protect the public, will be replaced with practices used by other countries, such as price controls, a ministry official said.
Since January 1996, foreigners have been free to own and to operate "value-added" services in the telecom sector such as Internet services and airline reservation systems.

In January 1997, Taiwan awarded eight lucrative mobile phone franchises to local consortiums, most of them paired with global telecom giants as minority partners -- whose ownership interest was capped at 20 percent.
